question: Explain how diffraction limits the ability of an optical instrument to distinguish two close objects. Use the expression for the angular limit of resolution and calculate it for an aperture of diameter $2.5\text{ cm}$ using light of wavelength $500\text{ nm}$.

options.A:
Diffraction makes the image of a point object spread into a pattern, so patterns of close objects can overlap and limit resolution. For a circular aperture, $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{1.22\lambda}{a}$.
With $\lambda=500\times10^{-9}\,\text{m}$ and $a=2.5\times10^{-2}\,\text{m}$, $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}}{2.5\times10^{-2}}=2.44\times10^{-5}\,\text{rad}$. A smaller value, obtained with larger aperture, means better resolution.
options.B: Diffraction improves resolution by making each point image perfectly sharp. $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{a}{1.22\lambda}=4.1\times10^4\,\text{rad}$.
options.C: The angular limit is $\Delta\theta=\dfrac{\lambda}{1.22a}=1.64\times10^{-5}\,\text{rad}$, and a smaller aperture gives better resolution.
options.D: Diffraction has no effect on resolution. For the aperture, the angular limit is $2.44\times10^{-3}\,\text{rad}$.
